text:
Unbrowse

 Your agent uses websites without a browser. 

Unbrowse runs on your own computer. The first time your agent needs something from a site, Unbrowse opens the page
once, finds the request the site's own app makes, and keeps it. After that, your agent makes that request directly:
plain HTTP, no browser, no page to read.

On a site it has learned, Unbrowse is up to 100× faster than driving a browser. Across 94 sites, an uncached answer took
950 ms on average, against 3,404 ms for a browser agent (research paper). A cached
answer comes back in about 67 ms.

 Install

Download the app for your computer:

 Your computer Download 
 --- --- 
 Mac with Apple silicon Unbrowse-13.21.0-installers.3-macos-arm64.dmg 
 Windows (x64) Unbrowse-13.21.0-installers.3-windows-x64-setup.exe 
 Linux, Debian or Ubuntu (x64) unbrowse 13.21.0-installers.3 amd64.deb 
 Linux, Debian or Ubuntu (ARM) unbrowse 13.21.0-installers.3 arm64.deb 

Every file with its SHA-256 is on the release; the step-by-step guide is at unbrowse.ai/ install.

Open the app. The Unbrowse window starts the node on your computer (its MCP server is 
then its Agents screen, the one it opens on, adds Unbrowse to the agents it finds (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor,
Codex, VS Code, Gemini CLI, opencode, Hermes, OpenClaw and 15 more, whichever are installed: the list)
and gives ChatGPT and Claude on the web an address for this node, with the steps to add it. No terminal, Node or npm.

- Mac: open the disk image and drag Unbrowse onto Applications. It is signed ad hoc, not notarized, so open it the
 first time by hand: right-click it and choose Open, or on macOS 15 and later, after the warning, System Settings 
 Privacy & Security Open Anyway.
- Windows: run the setup. It installs for your user alone, with no administrator prompt, and opens Unbrowse when it
 finishes. It is not code-signed, so SmartScreen asks once: More info, then Run anyway.
- Linux: sudo apt install ./unbrowse 13.21.0-installers.3 amd64.deb , then open Unbrowse from your apps menu. The window needs GTK 4.

These installers do not update themselves yet: download the newer one when it ships.

 Or with npm

You need Node 20.3 or newer, on macOS, Linux or Windows.

 

 unbrowse connect starts Unbrowse on your machine and adds it to Claude Code. Restart Claude Code and ask it to get
something from a website. unbrowse app opens the window; unbrowse start runs the node without it. For Codex,
Cursor, VS Code, Gemini, Zed and other agents, see Install the Unbrowse MCP.

npm fetches the programs for the machine it installs on: macOS (Apple silicon), Linux (x64 and arm64, glibc
2.35 or later) and Windows (x64). That brings the app, the node, unb , the agent skill and the client, and no browser:
the node fetches its browser the first time a goal needs one (or unbrowse browser install fetches it now;
docs/guides/the-browser.md). A full release, from npm or the
 unbrowse- -linux- .tar.gz and unbrowse- -windows-x64.zip archives on
Releases, keeps itself up to date and runs on Arc testnet. Foundry's Anvil ( foundryup ) is needed only for
test mode, the local devnet: the default of a build from source, or a node whose chain setting is devnet .

 Used the hosted version?

Unbrowse used to run on our servers. That service closed in November 2026. An old agent setup that still points at it hears the two
commands above in reply. If you set Unbrowse up with version 12 or earlier, run them. unbrowse connect finds your old
setup, asks before changing it, keeps a copy, and can undo the move. Logins you saved on the hosted service did not move
to your machine; Moving to the new Unbrowse says how to add the ones you need.

 How it works

A route is one learned call: the request, every value it needs traced to where it comes from, and the caller's
values as inputs. An agent says what it wants; the node calls the route that does it, or learns one and calls that.

 

Your sign-ins stay on your computer, in your system's own keystore.

 Choose a starting point

 Goal Start here 
 --- --- 
 Use it Install 
 Connect an agent (Claude Code, Cursor, …) Install the Unbrowse MCP, or Connect an agent 
 Move from the hosted version docs/upgrade.md 
 Build from this repo Run from source 
 Change the code The repository map, then the README.md in the directory you are touching 
 Understand the idea docs/concepts/: the concepts in plain words, from the papers, each ending with what the code does today and where it differs 
 Read the design papers/: the whitepaper, the economy, selection and the protocol specification, which is normative for the design 
 Understand how it works docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: the whole system with diagrams — pipeline, keys, peer network, payments; AGENTS.md for the pattern and rules 
 Know what it costs, and where fees go docs/MONEY.md: what each action costs, measured; the fee split; paying your own way 
 Start as a new owner, from install to first earnings docs/ONBOARDING.md; every command in docs/CLI.md; all the docs, and the order to read them, in docs/README.md 
 Fix something that broke docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: symptom, cause, fix 
 Contribute CONTRIBUTING.md; report vulnerabilities privately per SECURITY.md 

 Run from source

The node runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. Its root key lives in the system's keystore (the Keychain, Windows'
Credential Manager, or the Secret Service on Linux; on a Linux machine with no desktop session,
 /.unbrowse/root.key , readable by its user alone). The node browses in Chrome or any other Chromium browser on the
machine, and downloads Chrome for Testing the first time a goal needs a browser and there's none.

Toolchain, the versions CI pins (.github/workflows/ci.yml):

 Tool Version For 
 --- --- --- 
 Rust stable the node, unb , the browser 
 Foundry ( anvil ) latest ( foundryup ) test mode, the node's local payment chain

usage.title: Usage telemetry
usage.html:
The node tells Unbrowse how it is used, so we can show the network is used and fix what breaks. It is on by default in a release while the node is on the network (a node you keep off the network sends nothing; a build from source sends nothing unless UNBROWSE_TELEMETRY=1), it says so when it starts, and one command turns it off:

unbrowse-node telemetry off      # kept in ~/.unbrowse/telemetry.json; `unbrowse-node telemetry` shows the state
UNBROWSE_TELEMETRY=0             # in the environment: off, whatever the file says

What is sent, in batches to telemetry.unbrowse.ai (unbrowse-telemetry/), and nothing else:

Field What it is
event node_start (the node started), tool_call (an agent called a tool), route_failed (a route the node keeps ran and failed) or fetch_failed (a paid fetch of another node's route failed)
version, os the node's version, and macos, linux or windows
install_id a random id drawn once for this install. By itself it names no person, account, machine or name. If you link a wallet, the node's signed events to the site carry it too, joining this install's usage counts to that wallet.
tool which agent tool or API route: unbrowse_do, unbrowse_call, /v1/routes/{id}/call, … (never which route)
outcome, error_class ok, failed (the site's call failed) or error (the node refused it), and a coarse class: not_found, forbidden, site, …; for a failed route or fetch, the kind of failure from a fixed list (http, door, shape_mismatch, no_body, …)
duration_ms how long the call took
from on node_start only: the source tag the node was first started with, unbrowse start --from <tag> or UNBROWSE_FROM, such as hn-e (lowercase letters, digits and dashes); kept once in ~/.unbrowse/from.json

Never sent: URLs, sites or host names, page content, requests or answers, route ids, goals or inputs, cookies, passwords, passkeys, vault entries, keys, wallet addresses, user or machine names, or your IP address. Every field and value is checked against a fixed list before it is queued, and again by the worker, which refuses a batch with any other field or anything that looks like an address. The worker keeps each event and the hour it arrived; it never reads or keeps the caller's IP address.

Your linked wallet. If you link an optional wallet (with email or Google on unbrowse.ai, or your own; the node has its own), the node sends unbrowse.ai three signed events while telemetry is on: node_started, owner_linked and owner_unlinked (unbrowse-node/app/src/link.rs, link::tell). Each carries the node's address, your wallet, install_id, and, for unbrowse.ai sign-ins, your browser's visitor id (ub_vid, kept in ~/.unbrowse/owner.json) to trace the path from first visit to first good call and fix drop-offs. ub_vid needs Allow in the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland, has one-click Opt out elsewhere, and skips Global Privacy Control browsers. Visits join only through the site's own sign-in. Events never name a site, route or input, and telemetry.unbrowse.ai gets no wallet, site or visitor id. Unlinked nodes send none, outside wallet links send no ub_vid, turning telemetry off stops them, and opting out on unbrowse.ai/privacy deletes the joined data.

Source tag. Starting with unbrowse start --from <tag> or UNBROWSE_FROM=<tag> (such as hn-e) sends from on node_start while usage telemetry is on so Unbrowse can count which places send people who get a first working call. Everyone who copies an install line shares its visible tag, so it says where an install came from and never who made it. Valid tags are 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and dashes starting with a letter or digit, while anything else is ignored with a one-line warning and the node still starts. The node saves the first tag in ~/.unbrowse/from.json and never replaces it. Start without --from or UNBROWSE_FROM for no tag, or delete ~/.unbrowse/from.json to remove it.

Telemetry never slows the node: an event is queued without waiting, a full queue drops it, and a batch the worker doesn't take within a few seconds is dropped, never retried. With the worker down, everything works the same.
